spec.current_state: The menu-bar status item is a STATIC identity mark today: one SF Symbol `dot.radiowaves.left.and.right`, template-rendered, set once at init and never mutated by any app state (Sources/GithudApp/StatusItemController.swift:64-67). Left-click summons/toggles the island, right-click or Control-click opens the unified menu (StatusItemController.swift:114-127), and the WP-5i "Hide island / Show island" menu item exists (StatusItemController.swift:91-93, 129-135, 217) — its own doc comment marks the glyph as "unchanged (D-glyph is design-gated/excluded)" (StatusItemController.swift:214-216). Consequence: when the island is hidden, the user has ZERO ambient signal — every state cue lives only on the collapsed pill: count + most-urgent glyph, danger tint only when a critical row exists (CollapsedPillView.swift:83-96, tint decided at :91), the H2 segmented gauge when the inbox is clear (CollapsedPillView.swift:98-116), a bare tertiary-ink checkmark when fully clear (:117-123), a loading dot that never fakes "all clear" (:75-82), and a caution clock prepended when the reading is degraded (:67-73). The spoken value mirrors that exact priority — loading → "N need(s) you (, including a critical alert)" → gauge → "all clear", with "Reading may be stale." prepended when degraded (Sources/GithudCore/PillAccessibilityPresenter.swift:26-49). Critical is a single categorical reason, security_alert, which sorts critical-first so the top row IS the shield whenever one exists (Sources/GithudCore/SignalClassifier.swift:64-71, 183-186). Row shapes come from RadarPresenter.symbolName (Sources/GithudCore/RadarPresenter.swift:44-57). Freshness has three states — fresh / stale(age) / failing(consecutive, age) — and fresh renders no chrome (Sources/GithudCore/Freshness.swift:12-21). Geometry anchors: collapsed island 280×42, expanded 520×120, menu-bar gap 8 (Sources/GithudCore/IslandGeometry.swift:12-21); island corner radius 14 (Sources/GithudApp/HUDPanelController.swift:32); pill height 36, radius 14 (CollapsedPillView.swift:8, 44). GitHub theme palette for mocks: surface #0D1117, border #30363D, ink #E6EDF3/#7D8590/#484F58, accent #2F81F7, danger #F85149, success #3FB950, caution #D29922 (Sources/GithudApp/Theme.swift:111-119). Binding doctrine: ink by default, color only on a changed next-move, a11y gray-swap law (loop/INTENT.md iter-30 entry; loop/PRESSURE.md `color-doctrine`), motion only on real change (`attention-non-theft`), no permanent timers (`idle-footprint`). A template menu-bar image is alpha-only (system tints it black/white per bar appearance), so in this fourth surface the gray-swap law is not an audit — it is the physics: shape and fill weight must carry everything, including critical.
spec.design_question: When the island is hidden, how much of its signal should the ~18pt template glyph carry — and where does the action count live: knocked out inside the glyph, as adjacent real text, mirrored per-kind like the pill, or withheld entirely (tooltip/VoiceOver only)?

variants.name: Miniature Island (self-similar pill)
variants.essence: The menu-bar glyph IS the island in miniature — a hollow pill outline when clear that fills solid with a knocked-out count when GitHub needs you, teaching 'the island lives here' by pure self-similarity.
variants.spec: Status item: NSStatusItem.squareLength; template NSImage, canvas 18×18pt (36×36 @2x), isTemplate=true, alpha-only. STATE SET — (1) CLEAR: hollow pill, rect x=1.75 y=5.75 w=14.5 h=6.5 rx=3.25, fill=none, stroke-width=1.5 (outer silhouette x=1..17, y=5..13). (2) ACTION (count N ≥1): filled pill matching the hollow's OUTER silhouette exactly — rect x=1 y=5 w=16 h=8 rx=4, filled — with the count KNOCKED OUT (destination-out): system font semibold, font-size 6.75px, tabular numerals, centered at (9,9); N=1..9 shows the digit, N≥10 shows '9+' at font-size 5.75px. (3) CRITICAL (any row isCritical): same filled pill, knockout string '!'+N (e.g. '!3', font-size 6.25px, centered); N≥10 → '!' alone (bar 1.4×3.6 rounded r=0.7 at x=8.3 y=6.6, dot r=0.8 at (9,11.2)). The '!' is the emergency marker — shape-only, per the gray-swap law. (4) DEGRADED (freshness.isDegraded, composes over 1–3): stale ring — hollow circle center (14.75,3.25) r=2 stroke-width=1.25, sitting above the pill's top-right shoulder. One vocabulary item, always composable. (5) LOADING (pre-first-poll): the CLEAR hollow pill at alpha 0.40 — mirrors CollapsedPillView's never-fake-clear loading dot. STATE PRIORITY: loading → action/critical → clear; degraded composes onto any. TRANSITIONS: one-shot 180ms opacity crossfade, cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1), fired ONLY on state-class change (clear↔action↔critical, degraded toggle); a count-digit change within ACTION is a hard swap (0ms). Update trigger: model mutation on poll tick only — no timer, no loop. COPY: toolTip = "githud — {PillAccessibilityPresenter.value}. Click to expand, right-click for menu."; accessibilityDescription = same value string.
variants.doctrine_fit: Ink by default made literal (template = system ink); fill weight = the changed next-move ('filled/badged only when action is required' verbatim); '!' knockout carries critical with zero hue (gray-swap law is satisfied by construction); crossfade maps 1:1 to a real classifier change; no ambient motion, no timer (idle-footprint clean); self-similarity reinforces the summon affordance the hide feature needs.
variants.risks: Knockout digits are ~4.6px cap-height at 1x — the weakest 1x legibility of any variant; on a non-Retina external display the count may read as 'something' rather than '3' (mitigation is the cap at 9, but that's a patch, not a fix). '!3' at critical is two glyphs in a 14.5px-wide pill — dense. Silhouette changes between hollow and filled are subtle at a glance in a crowded menu bar.
variants.mock_notes: Self-contained HTML/CSS/JS. Menu-bar strips: height 24px; light bar background rgba(246,246,246,0.85) over a subtle wallpaper gradient, glyph color rgba(0,0,0,0.85); dark bar rgba(28,28,30,0.68), glyph rgba(255,255,255,0.85). Render each state as inline SVG viewBox='0 0 18 18' using fill/stroke: currentColor; knockout via <mask> (white pill rect, black <text x='9' y='9' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='central' font-family='-apple-system' font-weight='600' font-size='6.75'>3</text>). Show a 1x row (width=18) and 2x row (width=36, same viewBox) for all five states: clear / action(3) / critical(!3) / action+degraded / loading(opacity .4). State-toggle radio buttons + 'degraded' checkbox drive stacked absolutely-positioned SVG layers cross-fading with transition: opacity 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) — no CSS keyframe loops anywhere. Context panel below: GitHub-theme island — 280×42px, background #0D1117, 1px solid #30363D, border-radius 14px, menu-bar gap 8px, inner pill height 36px radius 14px, glyph #7D8590, count #E6EDF3 13px 600 tabular-nums — so the reviewer sees glyph and island as one language. Add a gray-swap proof row: every state rendered in flat #7D8590.

variants.name: Constant Beacon + Count-as-Text
variants.essence: The identity mark never moves — a radar beacon whose hollow center dot fills when you're needed, with the count as real 12pt text beside it, dashed arcs when the reading degrades, and a shield swap reserved for the one categorical emergency.
variants.spec: Status item: NSStatusItem.variableLength; template NSImage 18×18pt + button title. THE MARK (constant): center dot at (9,9) + one arc pair, all stroke-width 1.5, round linecaps. Left arc path 'M 5.9,12.1 A 4.4,4.4 0 0 0 5.9,5.9' (bulges left to x≈4.6); right arc 'M 12.1,5.9 A 4.4,4.4 0 0 0 12.1,12.1' (bulges right to x≈13.4). STATE SET — (1) CLEAR: hollow dot, circle cx=9 cy=9 r=2 stroke=1.5 fill=none; arcs solid; no title. (2) ACTION: dot fills — circle cx=9 cy=9 r=2.75 filled; arcs unchanged; button title = count as TEXT: NSFont.monospacedDigitSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .semibold), imagePosition=.imageLeading, image-to-title gap 3px; exact count 1–99, '99+' beyond. (3) CRITICAL: the whole mark swaps to a filled shield with knocked-out '!' — shield path 'M9,1.9 L14.6,4.1 C14.6,4.1 14.9,9.4 13.3,12.2 C11.9,14.6 9,16.1 9,16.1 C9,16.1 6.1,14.6 4.7,12.2 C3.1,9.4 3.4,4.1 3.4,4.1 Z' filled; knockout bar x=8.2 y=5.3 w=1.6 h=4.4 rx=0.8 + dot cx=9 cy=12 r=1 (mirrors the row set's exclamationmark.shield.fill); count text stays. Identity yields ONLY for the drop-everything case — exactly the classifier's own hierarchy. (4) DEGRADED (composes over 1–3 except critical, where it composes as dashed arcs beside the shield is omitted — shield alone outranks): arcs switch to stroke-dasharray 2.25 1.6 (round caps) — the radar's own arcs are the signal, so dashed arcs = degraded reading, a 1:1 semantic map to Freshness. (5) LOADING: entire mark at alpha 0.40, no title. TRANSITIONS: dot hollow↔filled and mark↔shield: one-shot 180ms opacity crossfade cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1); count text changes and dashed-arc toggles: hard swap 0ms (freshness degradation must never be celebrated with motion). Trigger: model change on poll tick only. COPY: title placeholder '{count}'; toolTip = "githud — {PillAccessibilityPresenter.value}. Click to expand, right-click for menu."
variants.doctrine_fit: Strongest findability story: menu-bar users locate items by silhouette, and this silhouette is constant except for the one emergency the doctrine says may interrupt. Count as real text is the only 1x-guaranteed-legible count treatment. Dashed-arcs = degraded reading reuses the ONE sanctioned caution meaning with shape, not hue. Fill-vs-hollow dot is the brief's 'calm hollow when clear, filled when action' verbatim. Zero ambient motion; template alpha only.
variants.risks: Variable width: the item widens when a count appears and narrows when clear — neighboring menu-bar items shift by ~10–18px on state change (a small, honest, but real layout jump; macOS Mail's badge does the same). The shield swap abandons the identity mark entirely at critical — deliberate, but the user must learn that the beacon 'becoming a shield' is still githud. Two visual channels (mark + text) cost ~30px of menu-bar real estate vs ~22px for square variants.
variants.mock_notes: Self-contained HTML/CSS/JS, same menu-bar strips as mini-island-pill (light rgba(246,246,246,0.85)/glyph rgba(0,0,0,0.85); dark rgba(28,28,30,0.68)/glyph rgba(255,255,255,0.85); bar height 24px). Item = flex row, gap 3px: inline SVG viewBox='0 0 18 18' (paths above, stroke/fill currentColor) + 3. Shield knockout via . Dashed arcs: stroke-dasharray='2.25 1.6' stroke-linecap='round'. States to render at 1x (18px) and 2x (36px): clear / action(3) / action+degraded(dashed arcs) / critical(shield+3) / loading(.4). Toggle UI cross-fades stacked layers 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) for class changes; the dashed-arc toggle and count changes swap with transition:none to demonstrate the 0ms rule. Demonstrate the width-jump honestly: put two fake neighbor items (wifi, battery glyph placeholders) beside it so reviewers see the reflow. Island context panel: 280×42px, #0D1117, 1px #30363D, radius 14px, gap 8px, count #E6EDF3, glyph #7D8590. Gray-swap proof row in #7D8590.

variants.name: Kind Promotion (the pill crosses the bar)
variants.essence: The menu-bar glyph mirrors the collapsed pill one-for-one: the top-urgency row's reason SHAPE plus a text count — the bar tells you not just that GitHub needs you, but what kind of need it is.
variants.spec: Status item: NSStatusItem.variableLength; template image 18×18pt + title. STATE SET — (1) CLEAR: hollow check-ring — circle cx=9 cy=9 r=6.25 stroke=1.5 fill=none + check path 'M 6.2,9.2 L 8.2,11.2 L 12,6.9' stroke=1.5 round caps/joins; no title. (2) ACTION: the TOP radar row's reason glyph, exactly RadarPresenter.symbolName's mapping (RadarPresenter.swift:44-57) rendered as SF Symbols, pointSize 13 weight .semibold, template: review_requested→arrow.triangle.pull, mention→at, team_mention→person.2.fill, assign→person.crop.circle.badge.checkmark, author→bubble.left.fill, invitation→envelope.fill, default→bell.fill; title = count, monospacedDigitSystemFont(12, .semibold), gap 3px, 1–99 then '99+'. (3) CRITICAL: exclamationmark.shield.fill 13pt semibold template + count — guaranteed consistent for free because critical sorts first (SignalClassifier.swift:183-186): the top row IS the shield. (4) DEGRADED (composes): an under-dash baked into the image — line from (4.5,16.75) to (13.5,16.75), stroke-width 1.5, stroke-dasharray 2 1.75, round caps, drawn beneath whichever glyph shows. (5) LOADING: dot.radiowaves.left.and.right 13pt regular at alpha 0.40 (mirrors CollapsedPillView.swift:75-82), no title. TRANSITIONS: class changes (clear↔action↔critical) one-shot 180ms crossfade cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1); a top-glyph change WITHIN action (e.g. review_requested absorbed, mention now tops) is a hard swap 0ms — legal motion but deliberately not spent; count and under-dash changes 0ms. Trigger: model change only. COPY: toolTip = "githud — {PillAccessibilityPresenter.value}. {reasonLabel(top)} first. Click to expand."
variants.doctrine_fit: 'Shape says what' applied maximally — the exact doctrine sentence, promoted to the fourth surface, with zero new vocabulary: the glyphs ARE the row glyphs, the sort IS the classifier's sort, critical-first makes shield-at-critical an invariant rather than a rule. Count as text passes 1x legibility. No hue, no ambient motion.
variants.risks: Findability is the honest casualty: the item's silhouette changes with the top row, so users can't lock onto a constant shape in a crowded bar — the strongest violation of menu-bar convention among the four. At 18pt/1x, at-sign vs bubble vs person-pair remain distinguishable but demand more attention per glance (a mild tension with attention-non-theft: it never steals attention, but it invites more of it than a binary cue). Duplicates the pill's job — if the island is usually visible, this surface is redundant chrome; its value exists only in the hidden-island mode it feeds.
variants.mock_notes: Self-contained HTML/CSS/JS, same two menu-bar strips (light rgba(246,246,246,0.85)/rgba(0,0,0,0.85); dark rgba(28,28,30,0.68)/rgba(255,255,255,0.85); 24px). SF Symbols aren't embeddable — approximate: at→@ centered; arrow.triangle.pull→path 'M5,3 A1.8,1.8 0 1 1 5,6.6 M5,6.6 L5,11.4 A1.8,1.8 0 1 0 5,15 M5,15 A1.8,1.8 0 1 1 5,11.4 M12.5,6 L12.5,11 M10.5,8 L12.5,6 L14.5,8' stroke 1.5 (a serviceable pull-request fork); bubble→rounded rect 3,4→15,12 rx=3 filled + tail triangle (6,12)(8,12)(6,15); shield→the shield path from constant-mark-count-text with '!' knockout; check-ring per spec. Count: 3, gap 3px. Under-dash: . Interactive: a dropdown of 'top row kind' (review/mention/author/critical) + degraded checkbox; class-change transitions 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1), within-action glyph swaps transition:none — make the 0ms-vs-180ms distinction visible with both controls. 1x/2x rows for: clear / action-review(2) / action-mention(1) / critical(1) / action+degraded / loading. Island context panel (#0D1117, #30363D, 280×42, radius 14, gap 8) showing the SAME top row in the pill so the mirroring reads. Gray-swap row in #7D8590.

variants.name: Binary Presence (count-free ring)
variants.essence: The bar answers exactly three questions and nothing else — am I needed (hollow vs filled), is it an emergency (knocked-out !), can I trust the reading (dashed halo) — the count is deliberately withheld to the tooltip and the click.
variants.spec: Status item: NSStatusItem.squareLength (constant width — the item NEVER reflows its neighbors); template image 18×18pt, no title ever. STATE SET — (1) CLEAR: hollow circle cx=9 cy=9 r=5.75 stroke-width=1.5 fill=none (outer silhouette r=6.5). (2) ACTION: filled circle cx=9 cy=9 r=6.5 — identical outer silhouette, pure weight change. (3) CRITICAL: filled circle r=6.5 with knocked-out exclamation — bar x=8.15 y=4.9 w=1.7 h=5.45 rx=0.85, dot cx=9 cy=12.35 r=1.05 (destination-out). (4) DEGRADED (composes over any state): outer dashed halo — circle cx=9 cy=9 r=8 stroke-width=1 stroke-dasharray 2.1 2.1 fill=none, alpha 0.9; the core state stays untouched inside it. (5) LOADING: the hollow circle at alpha 0.40. TRANSITIONS: every state change is a one-shot 180ms opacity crossfade cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1); there are no sub-state changes (no digits), so nothing else ever moves. Trigger: model mutation on poll tick only; no timers. COUNT CONTEXT (the brief's requirement, honored off-glass): toolTip = "githud — {PillAccessibilityPresenter.value}. Click to expand." (e.g. 'githud — 3 need you, including a critical alert.'); accessibilityDescription/value = the same presenter string, so VoiceOver hears exactly what the pill would say (PillAccessibilityPresenter.swift:26-49). The count's first-class home remains the island — one click, which this glyph summons.
variants.doctrine_fit: The calm ceiling: maximal attention-non-theft (a fill-weight change is the quietest possible 'you're needed'), constant width (zero layout churn — even quieter than today's static item ever gets to be under the other variants), trivially hue-free, silhouette-constant (findability perfect), and the three shapes map exactly onto the classifier's three interruption tiers: needed / emergency / don't-trust-the-reading.
variants.risks: Withholds the count — '1 needs you' and '7 need you' render identically, so the glyph answers 'whether' but never 'how much'; a user triaging by volume must click or hover. This is a philosophical bet that the ruthlessly-suppressed radar (≤5/day budget) makes counts low-value — if dogfooding shows count-at-a-glance matters when the island is hidden, this variant cannot grow one without becoming mini-island-pill. Hollow-vs-filled at 18pt in a crowded bar is subtle for peripheral vision (though that subtlety is arguably the point).
variants.mock_notes: Self-contained HTML/CSS/JS, same menu-bar strips (light rgba(246,246,246,0.85)/glyph rgba(0,0,0,0.85); dark rgba(28,28,30,0.68)/rgba(255,255,255,0.85); height 24px; item slot fixed 24px wide to demonstrate squareLength). Inline SVG viewBox='0 0 18 18', currentColor; exclamation knockout via <mask>; halo as a separate <circle r='8' stroke-dasharray='2.1 2.1' opacity='.9'>. Render 1x (18px) and 2x (36px) for: clear / action / critical / clear+degraded / action+degraded / loading(.4). Toggle UI (radio for class, checkbox for degraded) cross-fading stacked layers 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1); no keyframe loops. Simulate the tooltip: on hover after 800ms show a macOS-style tooltip div (background #2A2A2A, 1px rgba(255,255,255,.15), radius 4px, font 11px -apple-system, color rgba(255,255,255,.85), padding 3px 7px) reading 'githud — 3 need you, including a critical alert.' — the count lives there, make the reviewer feel that. Island context panel (#0D1117, border #30363D, 280×42, radius 14, gap 8px, ink #E6EDF3/#7D8590) beneath. Gray-swap proof row in #7D8590.

recommendation.why: It is the only variant that wins all three hard constraints at once: a constant silhouette (menu-bar findability — users locate items by shape, and this one only yields for the single categorical emergency the classifier itself defines), a count that is guaranteed legible at 1x because it is real 12pt text rather than sub-5px knockout digits, and a degraded-reading cue (dashed radar arcs) that maps the ONE sanctioned caution meaning to the mark's own semantics with zero hue. mini-island-pill is the better story but fails 1x count legibility; binary-presence is the calmer fallback if dogfooding shows counts don't matter when the island is hidden.

verdicts.reason: One genuine doctrine breach: LOADING is the CLEAR silhouette at alpha 0.40, and the spec's claim that this 'mirrors CollapsedPillView's never-fake-clear loading dot' is factually wrong — the code deliberately uses a DISTINCT neutral identity glyph (dot.radiowaves, CollapsedPillView.swift:75-82, comment: "DON'T claim 'all clear' (that would be a trust lie)"), never a dimmed clear shape. A dimmed hollow pill pre-first-poll is a softened 'all clear' the data can't back — the exact trap the record's own current_state names. Secondary: animating the degraded-ring toggle (180ms) contradicts the record's own strictest rule, stated in constant-mark-count-text ('freshness degradation must never be celebrated with motion') and PRESSURE attention-non-theft ('motion only on a real action-required change' — degraded is caution, not action). Everything else is clean: geometry is internally consistent (hollow outer silhouette = filled rect exactly), '!' knockout is shape-only, transitions map 1:1 to classifier changes, no timers, a11y wired to the real presenter. The sub-5px knockout-digit legibility risk is honestly declared and is a design-session question, not doctrine.
verdicts.amendment: LOADING must be a distinct non-clear mark — the identity glyph (dot.radiowaves-style) at alpha 0.40, or the pill outline with its interior dot only, never the bare CLEAR hollow pill dimmed — and delete the false 'mirrors the never-fake-clear loading dot' claim. Degraded stale-ring toggles at 0ms hard swap (crossfade reserved for clear↔action↔critical).

verdicts.reason: The DEGRADED-at-CRITICAL clause is garbled to the point of being unbuildable ('composes as dashed arcs beside the shield is omitted — shield alone outranks') and on its plainest reading — degraded omitted at critical — it hides a stale/failing reading exactly where trust matters most: the user sees a crisp shield backed by a reading that may be 20 minutes dead. That contradicts the code's own unconditional composition (CollapsedPillView.swift:67-73 prepends the caution clock over EVERY state; PillAccessibilityPresenter.swift:30-31 prepends 'Reading may be stale.' to every case including critical) and Freshness.swift's stated doctrine ('showing last-good as if it were live is the same faked-liveness trap'). Structurally, dashed-arcs-as-degraded dies at critical because the shield swap removes the arcs — the vocabulary breaks at its most important moment. Secondary: LOADING dims the whole mark including the hollow dot, and hollow-dot = the CLEAR cue, so loading is again a dimmed clear-signal. Otherwise strong: count-as-text is the only 1x-guaranteed count, the 0ms rule for count/freshness changes is the record's best motion discipline, width reflow is honest and mapped to a real change.
verdicts.amendment: Rewrite state (4) so degraded COMPOSES over critical: at critical+degraded render the dashed arc pair flanking the shield (arcs return as pure freshness chrome) or adopt mini-island-pill's corner stale-ring as the composable degraded token. LOADING renders arcs-only (no hollow dot) at alpha 0.40 so a dimmed clear-cue never shows pre-first-poll.

verdicts.reason: One softened-state breach: CLEAR = a hollow check-RING whenever the inbox is empty, but the pill's own bare check is gated on the H2 gauge being nil (CollapsedPillView.swift:98-123) — when active PRs exist the pill shows '✓ready · ⚠blocked', and this variant's own toolTip (PillAccessibilityPresenter) would speak 'N blocked' while the glyph asserts a checkmark. A check is a positive 'all good' claim the data can't always back — the glyph contradicts its own spoken value. Everything else is the cleanest in the record: LOADING correctly mirrors the code's actual treatment (dot.radiowaves at 0.40 — the only variant that gets this right), degraded under-dash composes over every state INCLUDING critical at 0ms, within-action glyph swaps are deliberately unanimated ('legal motion not spent'), shield-at-critical is verified an invariant (critical-first sort, SignalClassifier.swift:184-185; security_alert→exclamationmark.shield.fill, RadarPresenter.swift:52), and the symbol mapping quoted matches RadarPresenter.swift:44-57 exactly. The findability and attention-cost risks are honestly declared design tradeoffs, not doctrine violations.
verdicts.amendment: Reserve the check-ring for the pill's own bare-check condition (inbox clear AND PulsePresenter gauge == nil); when a gauge exists, render a neutral hollow ring without the check (meaning 'nothing needs you', not 'all clear') — or simply drop the check stroke from the CLEAR mark entirely.

verdicts.reason: Doctrinally the safest architecture of the four — constant silhouette, squareLength (zero reflow), the ONLY variant whose degraded cue (outer halo) composes over every state including critical by construction, three shapes mapping exactly to the classifier's three tiers, count honored off-glass via the real presenter string for tooltip AND VoiceOver (not hover-as-primary: click/island remains the count's first-class home and the spec says so). Two residual breaches, both shared-class: (1) LOADING is the CLEAR hollow circle at alpha 0.40 — a dimmed 'nothing needs you' shown before the first poll can back it, against the code's explicit refusal to reuse a clear-mark for loading (CollapsedPillView.swift:75-82); (2) 'every state change is a 180ms crossfade' includes the degraded-halo toggle, violating the record's own 0ms-for-freshness rule (stated in constant-mark-count-text) and the strict reading of attention-non-theft (motion only on action-required change; degraded is caution). The withheld-count bet is honestly framed with its own falsification condition (dogfood) and an admitted no-growth-path — acceptable as a design-session question.
verdicts.amendment: LOADING gets a distinct mark — the identity glyph at 0.40, or a lone small centered dot — never the dimmed CLEAR circle; degraded-halo toggles at 0ms hard swap, crossfade reserved for the clear↔action↔critical class changes.

review.overall_note: All current_state file:line citations verified accurate against source — no fabricated code claims in the record itself; the one false code claim is inside mini-island-pill's spec ('mirrors the never-fake-clear loading dot' — it doesn't; the code uses a distinct neutral glyph, CollapsedPillView.swift:75-82 with an explicit trust-lie comment). Three cross-variant patterns the session should settle ONCE, record-wide: (1) LOADING-as-dimmed-CLEAR-shape appears in three of four variants (only kind-promoted-glyph matches the code's actual never-fake-clear treatment) — adopt one loading mark rule; (2) motion on freshness degradation is inconsistent (constant-mark and kind-promoted hard-swap at 0ms, mini-island and binary-presence animate it) — adopt the 0ms rule everywhere per attention-non-theft; (3) ALL four variants omit H2's gauge from the glyph state set — defensible scoping (glyph answers H1 only; iter-27 keeps the axes orthogonal) but it means a hidden island shows no blocked-PR signal at all, and the session should make that call consciously, not by omission. RECOMMENDATION CHECK: constant-mark-count-text is NOT doctrine-safe as written — its degraded-at-critical clause is the record's worst trust hole (a stale reading hidden behind the shield) and must be amended before it is a defensible pick; its findability + 1x-legibility case is real, so AMENDED it is a legitimate recommendation. The strictly doctrine-safest variant is binary-presence (after its minor amendment): constant silhouette, degraded composes over everything, quietest possible signal — the recommendation should present amended constant-mark vs amended binary-presence as the live pair, with the count-at-a-glance question explicitly deferred to dogfooding. No variant warranted a kill: no ambient motion, no color misuse (template physics makes hue impossible), no hover-as-primary, no focus theft, no permanent timers, and every declared transition maps 1:1 to a real classifier/freshness change.
